newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pancanadian sees 90 mln bls oil in Venezuela area.
newsitem.headline: Pancanadian sees 90 mln bls oil in Venezuela area.

text.p: Pancanadian Petroleum expects to produce 90 million barrels of oil from the B2X.70/80 block in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo over 20 years, group vice-president Paul Ellis said Thursday.
Pancanadian won a contract to exploit the area in a 50/50 joint venture with Pennzoil, which earlier won the contract for neighbouring B2X.68/79 block.

Ellis said the consortium hopes to achieve production of 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) within four years, from 6,000 bpd now. He did not specify the investment required by the field, but said it would be much more than the minimum $17 million required under the contract with state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela.
Pancanadian/Pennzoil was the only consortium bidding for the block and won the contract with a bid of $1.3 million.
"There is no great exploration potential," Ellis said, although he would be evaluating this again in the future.

The consortium will receive a fee based on a complex formula, which participants say offers the contractor the chance to recoup their investment by raising production and then get 30 percent of the profits from any additional output, up to a pre-set ceiling.
Existing proven reserves in the B2X.70/80 field total 79 million barrels of medium density crude, but the consortium could be expected to increase this figure by using enhanced recovery techniques.
"The field is difficult because the sands are not very permeable and the sands are discontinuous, so it's difficult where the oil is going to move," Ellis added.
